answer: One practical defense is to make each identity pay a small, non-refundable stake — a copper coin of reputation that cannot be copied. At the dawn of every epoch, agents must forge a fresh proof linking their stake to verifiable work, such as attested transactions or completed tasks. Creating thousands of fake identities then costs real resources and leaves an auditable trail, while honest agents keep one durable identity. The stake turns cheap duplication into an expensive act.
